proposals.expected_failure_mode: Delay may be compensating for other dynamics (e.g., peak width), leading to split-to-split phase sensitivity and weak identifiability of the delay.
proposals.rationale: Anchor to previous best: fractional SEIRS with a 2-week observation delay to represent admissions lag while keeping dynamics parsimonious for a short, high-peaked series.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: May shift peaks earlier than observed, producing systematic lead bias and unstable performance across rolling splits if true lag is closer to 2 weeks.
proposals.rationale: Near-neighborhood delay test to assess robustness of peak timing when the admissions lag is shorter; maintains identical structure to isolate delay effect.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: May over-lag the peak and smear the decline, degrading fit around turning points and increasing generalization gap if lag is not truly that long.
proposals.rationale: Near-neighborhood delay test to assess robustness when admissions lag is longer; helps probe whether delay is under-identified in this series.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: H-state parameters may be weakly identifiable in a short single-season series, causing parameter drift and unstable peak height/width across splits.
proposals.rationale: Minimal explicit-hospitalization baseline (H observed) to test whether adding an H compartment improves stability across splits versus delay-only observation, without adding extra mapping complexity.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: Added flexibility may still not resolve H identifiability; could overfit peak sharpness and yield inconsistent rolling-split behavior.
proposals.rationale: Fractional SEIHR baseline to allow heavier-tailed/peaky dynamics while still directly observing H; tests whether fractional dynamics reduce peak-timing sensitivity relative to standard SEIHR.
